Welcome back to PharmacyInsider.

Today I want to talk about one of the 

most well known vitamins — but also 

one of the most misunderstood ones.

Vitamin C.

After three years working in a pharmacy 

in Qatar, Vitamin C is one of the most 

consistently purchased supplements I see. 

But most customers do not fully understand 

what it actually does, how much they need, 

and what happens when they do not get 

enough.

Let me explain everything clearly.

---

What Makes Vitamin C Different?

First — something very important that 

most people do not know.

Vitamin C is a water soluble vitamin.

This means unlike Vitamin D or Vitamin A 

which are fat soluble and stored in your 

body — Vitamin C cannot be stored.

Your body uses what it needs and flushes 

out the rest through urine every single 

day.

This is why you need Vitamin C daily — 

not just once a week or occasionally.

---

What Vitamin C Actually Does For 

Your Body

Vitamin C works across multiple systems 

in your body simultaneously:

1. Boosts Immune System

Vitamin C is one of the most powerful 

natural supporters of your immune system. 

It stimulates the production of white 

blood cells which fight infections and 

bacteria. This is why people reach for 

Vitamin C at the first sign of a cold.

2. Heals Wounds Faster

Vitamin C is essential for collagen 

production. Collagen is the protein that 

forms the structure of your skin, tendons, 

and connective tissue. Without enough 

Vitamin C your wounds heal significantly 

slower.

3. Keeps Skin Healthy

Because of its role in collagen production 

Vitamin C directly affects your skin 

quality. It helps maintain skin structure 

and elasticity. This is why Vitamin C is 

found in so many skincare products.

4. Supports Bone and Blood Vessel Health

Vitamin C helps maintain the integrity of 

your blood vessels and contributes to 

healthy bone formation. People with 

chronically low Vitamin C often experience 

joint pain and weakness.

5. Helps Your Body Absorb Iron

This is something I tell customers 

regularly — if you take iron supplements, 

take them with Vitamin C. Vitamin C 

dramatically increases the absorption of 

non-heme iron from plant sources. This is 

especially important for vegetarians and 

vegans.

---

Signs You May Be Vitamin C Deficient

In my pharmacy experience, customers 

who come in with these symptoms are 

often found to be low on Vitamin C:

⚠️ Bleeding gums — one of the earliest 

 and most common signs

⚠️ Slow healing wounds

⚠️ Constant fatigue and weakness

⚠️ Frequent infections and illness

⚠️ Dry rough skin

⚠️ Joint and muscle pain

⚠️ Easy bruising

Severe Vitamin C deficiency leads to 

a condition called Scurvy — which causes 

extreme fatigue, severe gum bleeding, 

tooth loss, and skin problems. While 

rare today, I still see cases of mild 

deficiency regularly.

---

About Vitamin C Supplements

When customers ask me about Vitamin C 

supplements I always share these points:

1. More is not always better

Your body can only absorb a limited 

amount of Vitamin C at once — roughly 

200 to 400mg per dose. Very high doses 

like 1000mg or more are mostly wasted 

and excreted through urine. Smaller 

doses taken regularly work better.

2. Timing matters

Take Vitamin C with meals for better 

absorption and to reduce any stomach 

discomfort.

3. Different forms available

Ascorbic acid is the standard form and 

works well for most people. Buffered 

Vitamin C is gentler on the stomach 

for people who experience digestive 

issues with regular ascorbic acid.

4. Who benefits most from supplements

People who smoke — smoking depletes 

Vitamin C rapidly. People with poor 

diets low in fruits and vegetables. 

People recovering from illness or 

surgery. People under chronic stress.

---

Vitamin C and Iron — Important 

Connection

I want to highlight this again because 

it is so practically useful.

If you read my earlier post about Iron 

deficiency you will know that non-heme 

iron from plant sources has poor 

absorption.

Taking Vitamin C alongside iron rich 

plant foods or iron supplements can 

increase absorption by up to 67%.

Simple example: Eat lentils with 

tomatoes. Take your iron supplement 

with orange juice. These small habits 

make a significant difference.

---

My Honest Pharmacy Observation

Vitamin C is genuinely one of the most 

useful supplements available — but only 

if you need it. If you eat plenty of 

fresh fruits and vegetables daily you 

are likely getting enough.

Where I see real benefit is in customers 

who have poor diets, work long indoor 

shifts, smoke, or are recovering from 

illness. For these people a simple daily 

Vitamin C supplement makes a noticeable 

difference.
